name: Select field
summary: Pick one value from a short, known set — a lightweight native-select-backed field that embeds anywhere.
lead: ONE custom element — <aha-select> — defined once, imported unchanged by React and Vue. It is the LEAF counterpart to the composite Select: instead of a popup + virtualised list, it is a styled control backed by a NATIVE <select>, so it inherits the OS keyboard model, focus and a11y for free — no custom listbox, no roving to hand-roll. CSS lives in the shadow DOM, so both frameworks render byte-identical pixels; theming comes only from --aha-* tokens. Use it to pick one value from a short set and — crucially — to embed a select in a shadow-DOM row (aha-settings-list's control.type "select"), where the composite can't reach. The open dropdown is a fully THEMED role="listbox" popup (DS surface, radius 8, elevation shadow, brand-tinted hover + a check on the selected option) — not the browser's native <select> list; it's an accessible combobox (Arrow/Home/End, typeahead, Enter/Escape, outside-click).

spec.label: Popup
spec.value: themed role=listbox — white surface, radius 8, elevation shadow, brand-tint hover, check on selected; Arrow/Home/End + typeahead + Escape; outside-click close

props.name: placeholder
props.desc: Dimmed hint shown when no value is selected

props.name: open
props.desc: Reflects/controls the themed listbox popup being open (also toggled by click/keyboard). aria-expanded stays in sync.

whenToUse.when: one value from a short, known set (≤ ~10), or a select inside a shadow-DOM surface like a settings row — no search/tags/multi needed
a long list needing type-to-search, multiple/tags, async loading, or option groups
2–5 mutually-exclusive options all worth showing at once

opinion.note: Pre-select the recommended default rather than leaving it empty. Keep option labels short and sentence case; keep product nouns — Q&A, Word cloud. This is the leaf half of the hybrid — reach for the composite Select the moment you need search, tags, or a virtualised list.
opinion.dsv3: COVERED — the DS V3 select chrome measured against the Select component set on fileKey MwjvUjVI0HnfwD9EwPXRAy: control 32 · radius 8 · 1px border #E3E3E3, size axis small 24 / default 32 / large 40, brand #6A1EBB focus border, #8A8A8A placeholder, status error #F5222D / warning #FF7747. This is the native-<select>-backed LEAF form of that chrome (the composite Select carries the popup/search/tags axes). Token layer: white surface, border #E3E3E3, hover border-hover #D3B4FF, disabled bg-container-disabled #F1F1F1 / border-disabled #EBEBEB. a11y: a native <select> carries the full OS keyboard + AT contract for free — no custom listbox/roving to hand-roll; the border/focus transition lives on a PERSISTENT wrapper (a `_focused` attribute toggles; the <option> list repopulates in place, the transition node is never rebuilt). The trailing caret is summoned by name via <aha-icon name="system-caret-down">, never an inline glyph.

a11y.role: the native <select> carries its own combobox/listbox semantics — no ARIA to bolt on
a11y.keyboard: native — the OS drives it: Space/Enter opens, Up/Down move, type-ahead jumps, Esc closes; the <select> is the tab stop
a11y.note: Backing the field with a real <select> inherits the platform keyboard model and screen-reader support for free, and dodges the roving-listbox burden a hand-rolled popup would carry. The wrapper is decorative chrome (aria-hidden caret); the field is the control.

codeNote: Same element, same shadow-DOM CSS → identical render. The only per-framework code is binding glue (React < 19 needs the ref wrapper to set `options` as a property; Vue binds `:options.prop` natively). The primitive is defined once in @ahaslides-product/design.

selfCheck.label: native <select> — OS keyboard + AT for free

conformance.$about: Measured by qa.mjs against the RENDERED UI (getComputedStyle via headless CDP). Leaf = ONE shared element, so there is a single render (no per-framework roots). The probe is a placeholder (value-less) <aha-select>.
